correctness.rationale: For a distinct new point, transitivity in its three possible positions gives precisely the ideal condition on L, filter condition on U, and strict comparability l<u for every mixed pair. These suffice for the old induced order to stay unchanged. Universality plus homogeneity realizes each diagram over the named base and makes it a complete type. For pure profiles the ideal polynomials count the possibilities directly; an ideal is specified by its selected minimal elements and an arbitrary subset of maximal elements with all predecessors selected. If both profiles are nonempty then L lies in the lower shore, U in the upper shore, and they induce a complete bipartite subgraph. A tree has no four-cycle, so one shore is a singleton. The two degree sums double-count only the n−1 edges, which explains the st correction. The closed form uses the height-two convention of two disjoint shores (n≥2, as in the census). Independently generated rooted trees as multisets of rooted branches, deduplicated unrooted and shore-coloured trees by canonical codes minimized over all choices of root, and counted profiles by allowed strict relations rather than the degree formula. This reproduces every census row through ten, including 106 free trees, 203 oriented classes, 201 polynomials and exactly the two stated size-two fibres. Direct coefficient checks match H0, H1 and the mixed terms, including 332 and 340 totals. Reversing the colours distinguishes the dual pair and fixes each of the other two isomorphism classes; the latter have different uncoloured codes.
residual_risks: No claim is made about the fibre census after order ten or the formula for cover graphs with cycles. Under an at-most-two convention the singleton should instead be treated separately, with type polynomial 1+s+t.

originality.rationale: Credit the standard insertion constraints, prior scalar tree-cover counting, and the broader reconstruction through seven; do not claim them as new. The supported distinct claim is the exact height-two tree formula and sharp restricted cutoff, with complete first collision fibres, exhibiting both reversal and tree-shape ambiguity. The closest broader result uses the same polynomial but its eight-point census on all posets does not establish the target's order-nine injectivity or order-ten fibre classification. No priority order is inferred from same-day catalogue dates.
residual_risks: Pretzel's full paper and the full texts of the most relevant catalogue comparisons were not available in the attempted retrievals.
An exact hidden census for the equivalent shore-degree and ideal-enumerator invariant is not ruled out by the comparisons. Historical priority is provisional.

value.rationale: The object class is natural: its tree incidence both controls mixed extensions and allows nontrivial orientation. The first failure and complete fibres distinguish two genuinely different losses of information: inability to identify orientation and inability even to identify tree shape. The all-order expression links the invariant to reusable ideal counts and degree data rather than providing an arbitrary list of examples.
residual_risks: Value rests on the restricted boundary and equality classification, not on rediscovering the scalar formula or the general injectivity range through seven.
